scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, not a bill-accuracy problem, so an auto-answering agent would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused systematically incorrect bills (e.g. wrong estimate substitution or read acceptance logic), driving disputes.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: A degradation in the vendor-run AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) since August caused missing or invalid interval reads, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: The contracted manual meter-read handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded since August (missed uploads or incomplete routes), increasing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: MeterWorks (ORG-FIELD) lacks sufficient contracted headcount to complete read routes, causing missed reads that get estimated and disputed.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: An error in billing import validation or tariff application produces incorrect bills even when the underlying meter read is ACTUAL, accounting for the majority (1785 of 3025) of disputed bills.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even when the read was received on time and exported, forcing estimate substitution for 1184 of 1240 estimate-based disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-01 shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 on ESTIMATED reads and 1785 on ACTUAL reads (3025 total). The majority of disputes are tied to bills built on ACTUAL (not estimated) reads, so read-failure/estimate-substitution causes can explain at most the minority (1240) of disputed bills; something else drives disputes even when a real meter read was used.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff rate changes are logged, so the hypothesized billing errors cannot be attributed to a tariff change event; the import-validation-logic explanation for ACTUAL-read billing errors remains untested by this query.

Field route-log shows manual read route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target for the 2026-08..09 period, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — i.e. field crews fell short of target coverage during the dispute-surge window, a plausible but modest contributor to incomplete manual reads.

E-04 shows CRM dispute response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA — response handling is comfortably within target, not degraded. This undercuts the premise that the dispute surge is caused by slow ticket response that an auto-answer agent would fix.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder statement that agrees with the already-recorded authoritative tool result E-02 (tariff_change_log_count=0) rather than adding new information.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, has a headcount incentive) claims a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes and estimated bills for affected customers. Per E-01, estimated-read bills are only the minority (1240/3025) of disputes, so even if accurate this mechanism cannot be the primary driver of the dispute surge.

E-07 (crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly) shows monthly dispute counts of 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09): volume roughly doubled starting August (1180/590≈2.0, 1260/610≈2.1), confirming the magnitude of the surge referenced in the initial request but saying nothing about what causes it.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document confirms the authority structure already encoded in constraint K-DISPATCH: route priority changes (push_route_update) require Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) runtime confirmation before execution; it is procedural/authority evidence, not causal evidence about the dispute surge.

This is route-level detail supporting the W-WI-2 estimate-substitution analysis on the DA-ROUTE side only; it carries no read-type, tariff, or account linkage.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (Telemetrix AMI Program Engineer) states MDMS export access for Lakeside is now provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which if true would lift the ACCESS_PENDING hold that previously blocked querying mdms-export for the estimate-substitution analysis (U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE / DA-MDMS). This is a stakeholder claim about data access, not a causal finding about dispute cause.

E-12 breaks down the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills by AMI read channel into two groups: 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION by billing import, forcing estimate substitution; only 56 (4.5%) show a genuine NO_READ_RECEIVED/export failure. All 1240 records are read_channel AMI, so none of this population traces to field manual-read failures. The dominant driver of estimate substitution is thus the same billing-import validation logic rejecting valid reads, not AMI export delivery degradation or field route lag.

U-IMPORT-DEFECT-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What specific defect in billing import validation or tariff-application logic produces incorrect bills on ACTUAL meter reads?
U-IMPORT-DEFECT-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Must be identified and documented before any bill-correction action can be proposed; determines which billing-config change is the fix target.
U-IMPORT-DEFECT-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) and correlate flagged rule/validation changes to the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed accounts' import timestamps.
U-IMPORT-DEFECT-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Produce a documented defect hypothesis with cited evidence; do not execute any bill write until the defect is confirmed and a separate SH-BILL-authorized correction process is engaged.

U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE.question: Is the minority of estimate-based disputes (1240 of 3025) driven by field manual-read failures (H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE), AMI/MDMS export delivery degradation (H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE), or both?
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether the estimated-read minority needs a separate fix track (field process vs AMI vendor delivery) alongside the ACTUAL-read defect fix.
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query MDMS read-event log and route-log completion data for the disputed ESTIMATED-read accounts and compare timing to H-FIELD-BILL/H-MDMS-BILL delivery records.
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat the estimated-read minority (1240/3025) as a secondary, lower-priority track; do not block the ACTUAL-read defect diagnosis on resolving it.
U-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-CAUSE.resolution: Dominant mechanism (1184/1240, 95.5%) is billing import rejecting valid, on-time, exported AMI high-consumption reads, not AMI/MDMS export delivery degradation (56/1240, 4.5%) and not field manual-read failure (0 of the AMI-channel-only population).

U-BASELINE-DEFINITION.question: What is the correct pre-August baseline dispute volume to judge recovery against — the June/July average (~600) or a longer historical window?
U-BASELINE-DEFINITION.decision_impact: Determines the exact target threshold used to judge whether dispute-volume recovery (SC-DISPUTE-VOLUME-REDUCTION) has succeeded.
U-BASELINE-DEFINITION.resolution_path: Confirm baseline with SH-CS/SH-BILL using the longer historical crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly series.
U-BASELINE-DEFINITION.safe_placeholder: Use the June-July average (~600/month) as provisional baseline per F-06.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.question: Is Telemetrix vendor-provisioned MDMS export access available, or does the ACCESS_PENDING hold on mdms-export (DEGRADED) persist?
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.decision_impact: Blocks direct AMI read-event queries for the estimate-substitution analysis; without it only route-log (manual-read) data is available.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.resolution_path: ORG-AMI (vendor) provisions export access per DA-MDMS acquisition note; retry mdms-export once tool_health reports HEALTHY.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with DA-ROUTE-only analysis of the estimate-substitution minority until mdms-export access is restored.
U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS.resolution: This AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE mdms-export query succeeded, confirming vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is now available (agreeing with CL-04/E-11).
